title: FedSC: Federated Learning with Semantic-Aware Collaboration

problem.claim: Federated learning faces data heterogeneity caused by biased labeling preferences across clients.

gap.claim: Existing methods often neglect semantic information inherent in each client when addressing data heterogeneity.

contributions.claim: FedSC captures client-specific and class-relevant knowledge across heterogeneous clients through semantic-level relational and consistent prototypes.
FedSC uses inter-contrastive learning to align instance embeddings with same-semantics relational prototypes and separate them from distinct classes.
FedSC constructs consistent prototypes through discrepancy aggregation to regularize the local model's optimization region.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report providing a theoretical analysis that ensures a convergence guarantee.
The authors report that experiments on various challenging scenarios demonstrate FedSC's effectiveness and the efficiency of its crucial components.
The authors provide an implementation through a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning trains models collaboratively without sharing client data for privacy preservation.
Client data heterogeneity, especially biased labeling preferences, remains a major challenge.
FedSC addresses the challenge by collaboratively modeling semantic-level relational and consistent prototypes.
Inter-contrastive learning handles relational prototypes, while discrepancy aggregation produces consistent prototypes as local regularization.
The abstract reports convergence analysis and experimental effectiveness across challenging scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Semantic information within each client can be represented through relational and consistent prototypes.

interpretation.claim: Prototype-wise collaboration may expose class-relevant structure that client-agnostic aggregation misses.

application.claim: In heterogeneous collaborative learning, consider sharing or aligning semantic prototypes alongside model parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which data distributions, label regimes, or deployment settings may limit this approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the evaluated datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or scenario definitions.
The abstract does not provide the form or assumptions of the convergence guarantee.
The abstract does not describe communication cost, privacy properties beyond the federated-learning setting, or reproducibility details.
